_comment: Milestone 7: IE-CoR, 40 modern Indo-European languages, 170 concepts. Ages in years before AD 2000. STATUS: DRAFT. These clade ages are broad ranges from the historical record, written for a comparison between cognate codings under identical calibrations; they are not Heggarty et al.'s (2023) calibrations (which use ancient tip dates) and must be reviewed before any Indo-European date is quoted.

root_age._why: Broad: contains both the Steppe (c. 6000 BP) and Anatolian (c. 8000-9500 BP) hypotheses with margin; the lower bound is just above the Indo-Iranian minimum.

loss_rate._why: As milestone 5: basic-vocabulary replacement of roughly 10-30% per millennium.

calibrations.name: Romance
calibrations.source: Latin still a single literary and spoken standard in the late Republic; Romance differentiation from the late Empire (Dacia abandoned AD 271) to the earliest Romance texts (9th century). DRAFT.

calibrations.name: NorthGermanic
calibrations.source: Old Norse largely uniform in the Viking Age; Iceland settled c. AD 870; East/West Norse distinct by c. AD 1000-1100. DRAFT.

calibrations.name: Slavic
calibrations.source: Late Common Slavic dialect continuum until c. AD 600-800; Old Church Slavonic (9th century) still close to the common language. DRAFT.

calibrations.name: Baltic
calibrations.source: East Baltic split conventionally placed in the first millennium AD. DRAFT.

calibrations.name: IndoIranian
calibrations.source: Distinct Indo-Aryan (Mitanni names, c. 1400 BC; early Vedic) and Iranian (Old Avestan) by the mid-second millennium BC. DRAFT.

calibrations.name: Celtic
calibrations.source: Primitive Irish (Ogham, from c. 4th century AD) already distinct from British. DRAFT.
